items.impact: Unknown top-level evidence fields are rejected, giving consumers a stable closed-world envelope.
items.statement: The evidence bundle is a Draft 2020-12 object with a fixed identifier, a fixed title, a closed top-level property set, and an explicit required-field list.
items.title: Closed root evidence envelope

items.impact: Consumers cannot infer that web or runtime-route activity was absent merely because their optional evidence blocks are absent; omission and no activity are indistinguishable.
items.statement: The root required list terminates after checks and does not require the later web_activity or runtime_route_action_evidence properties, leaving no explicit present-but-empty or not-applicable state for those evidence families.
items.title: Optional activity blocks conflate absence with no activity

items.impact: The bundle can carry normalized evidence for search, provider configuration and routing, reads, extraction, research, crawl, and map operations.
items.statement: web_activity is a closed optional object that exposes typed receipts for multiple web-operation and provider-routing families.
items.title: Normalized web activity evidence family

items.impact: A websearch results array can contain empty objects, so a result can count as present without a title, URL, snippet, or source type and cannot be reliably consumed or falsified.
items.statement: The search-result item object declares candidate properties but no required member or minimum identifying content.
items.title: Search results permit empty evidence objects

items.impact: Invalid, non-URL, local, or otherwise disallowed targets remain schema-valid; validation and redirect-policy enforcement are left entirely outside this evidence oracle.
items.statement: Although the requested URL is described as validated, url and final_url are only strings and carry no URI format, scheme allowlist, host policy, or redirect-chain structure.
items.title: URL validation is prose-only

items.impact: Every valid bundle has at least one typed event reference, preserving a minimum trace anchor even when other evidence arrays are empty.
items.statement: The required events object contains a non-empty event_refs array whose entries require a source enum and non-empty reference.
items.title: Evidence bundles require an event trace anchor

evidence.exact_quote: "description": "Run Graph HITL actions consume Plans/Run_Graph_View.md and /Run_Graph_View.md command evidence: cmd.graph.approve_hitl and cmd.graph.deny_hitl use { node_id: string, rationale: string }."

items.impact: Empty HITL, widget, workspace-isolation, runtime-native, and shared-payload evidence objects validate, so approval, denial, isolation, routing, and confirmation claims can exist without their described identifiers or rationale.
items.statement: runtime_route_action_evidence and each nested action-argument object are closed but declare no required fields, despite descriptions using must-level route and HITL contracts.
items.title: Runtime action evidence permits empty claims

items.impact: A route-aware verification can report PASS while any or all verification booleans are false and all detail arrays are empty, allowing a misleading acceptance receipt.
items.statement: The GATE-010 result enum is not conditionally coupled to the five verification booleans or to non-empty corresponding detail evidence.
items.title: GATE-010 PASS can contradict its verification facts

items.impact: Non-user initiation cannot validate without a non-empty reason, improving accountability for autonomous operations.
items.statement: InvocationProvenance conditionally requires agent_reason for agent_initiated, goal, PRD, planning-wizard, and subagent invocation sources.
items.title: Automated invocations require a rationale

items.impact: A cache hit can omit both cache_ref and content_hash, and non-stored states can carry storage-only fields; consumers cannot prove identity, provenance, expiration, or coherent cache lifecycle.
items.statement: CacheRecord only specializes the stored state; it does not impose state-specific requirements or exclusions for hit, miss, bypassed, or not_stored, and stored permits ttl_seconds equal to zero.
items.title: Cache lifecycle states lack coherent evidence invariants

items.impact: Schema-valid citations must represent more than provider snippets and must bind extract or read-like evidence kinds to the corresponding receipt reference.
items.statement: CitationRecord requires snippet_only to be false and conditionally requires extract_receipt_ref or read_receipt_ref according to evidence_kind.
items.title: Citations reject snippet-only evidence

items.impact: Denied jobs may lack any finish time or reason, and cancelled jobs require a finish time but no cancellation reason; terminal audit trails are non-uniform and can be non-diagnostic.
items.statement: WebOperationJob requires finished_at_utc for completed, failed, cancelled, and timeout, but excludes denied; only failed and timeout require failure_reason_code.
items.title: Denied and cancelled jobs have incomplete terminal evidence

items.impact: Arbitrary operation inputs remain valid, while success true need not carry a result and success false need not carry a denial or failure reason; operation receipts are weak acceptance oracles.
items.statement: WebActionResult constrains operation_input only to an object containing matching web_operation and tool_id, with no closed or operation-specific argument schema, and success is not conditionally coupled to result or failure evidence.
items.title: Web action inputs and outcomes are underconstrained

items.impact: Unknown source metadata bypasses the otherwise closed evidence vocabulary, creating silent producer-consumer drift and an uncontrolled place for sensitive or untrusted provider fields.
items.statement: ResearchSource explicitly allows arbitrary additional properties, unlike adjacent evidence definitions that reject unknown fields.
items.title: Research sources reopen the closed evidence model

items.impact: A compare, synthesize, or closure-check step can claim an output with no source inputs, preventing consumers from proving lineage or coverage.
items.statement: ResearchSynthesisStep requires input_source_refs as a field but gives the array no minItems and does not require receipt or citation references for any step kind.
items.title: Synthesis steps can have empty provenance

items.impact: Completed subagent records can lack results, failed records can lack reasons, terminal records can lack finish times, and nonterminal records can carry them, making orchestration evidence ambiguous.
items.statement: ResearchSubagentRecord enumerates lifecycle status but does not conditionally require or prohibit result_ref, failure_reason_code, or finished_at_utc according to status.
items.title: Subagent lifecycle states are internally contradictory

items.impact: Every research run must expose at least one selected source, one read receipt, and one non-snippet citation before it can validate.
items.statement: ResearchRun requires non-empty sources, read_receipts, and citations arrays, creating a baseline evidence floor.
items.title: Research runs require source, read, and citation evidence

items.impact: A run can claim sufficient closure without synthesis or a coverage report, while failed, denied, or cancelled runs need no reason; closure is declarative rather than demonstrable.
items.statement: ResearchRun does not condition closure_state on synthesis_steps, coverage_report_ref, or failure_reason_code and does not establish referential integrity among sources, receipts, citations, and synthesis references.
items.title: Research closure can be asserted without closure proof

items.impact: Consumers can distinguish deep-research records through a schema-enforced mode invariant while retaining the base ResearchRun contract.
items.statement: DeepResearchRun composes ResearchRun and constrains mode to the deep constant.
items.title: Deep research is a strict mode specialization

segments.summary: Reviewed the root schema identity, closed-world object contract, and required evidence envelope; identified omission ambiguity for optional activity evidence families.
Reviewed all web activity, provider, fetch, crawl, and map evidence fields; found empty search results and prose-only URL validation.
Reviewed runtime action evidence and core bundle receipts, events, files, artifacts, checks, and GATE-010; found unenforced action payloads and contradictory PASS states.
Reviewed invocation, cache, read receipt, and citation definitions; confirmed agent rationale and non-snippet citation gates while finding incoherent cache-state evidence.
Reviewed web job, action result, research source, and synthesis-step definitions; found incomplete terminal states, open inputs and source metadata, and empty synthesis provenance.
Reviewed research subagent, run, closure, and deep-mode contracts; confirmed the minimum evidence floor and deep specialization while finding invalid subagent and closure-state combinations.

cross_document_questions: Which canonical runtime contract makes PASS depend on every GATE-010 verification fact being true and supported by non-empty details?
Which owner defines state-specific terminal, failure, cancellation, and denial evidence for web jobs and research subagents?
Where is referential integrity among research sources, read receipts, citations, synthesis steps, and closure reports enforced?
Which security contract defines allowed URL schemes, redirect policy, private-network handling, redaction, retention, and deletion for web evidence?
research_queries: JSON Schema 2020-12 patterns for conditionally coupling PASS results to boolean evidence and non-empty detail arrays
JSON Schema lifecycle invariants for queued running completed failed cancelled timeout and denied jobs
Evidence schema referential-integrity patterns for sources receipts citations synthesis steps and closure reports
Secure URL evidence schemas for redirect chains private-network restrictions redaction retention and deletion
